_comment: rock_bars: A CAVE WALL WITH SLOTS, not a row of bars (Ryan: "less like carved bars and more like a cave wall with slots through it"). One mass of the map's own hell rock spans the 10.6 x 8.5 m gallery cross-section -- no sill, no lintel, no uprights -- its two faces swelling and thinning on their own (half-thickness 0.115 .. 0.50 m, heaviest at the haunch into the floor and under the brow at the crest, so the wall is 0.23 m through at its thinnest and 1.00 m at its deepest), its last band under the ceiling broken rather than sawn (up to 0.42 m, line by line; the top row itself is dead flat at 8.5 because map_base's gallery ceiling is exactly CEIL_H 8.5 m over the deck and a knocked-out crest would be a letterbox of daylight over the gate). Eight slots are cut clean through it, no two alike: each has its own width, lean, kink, taper and its own head and foot, and the rock left between them is never under ROCK_MIN 0.50 m (below that a column stops being a mass and starts being a bar) with the spare width piled onto two or three real masses by ROCK_SKEW rather than shared out evenly -- 0.41 .. 1.40 m as built, so the screen has no rhythm to read off. Every row of the lattice carries its own x and z wobble, which is what makes a cut edge ragged instead of milled. THE GUARANTEE IS UNCHANGED: no opening exceeds 0.48 m at any height (world), so a body (0.8 m across) cannot pass and a rifle round and a sight line can -- tools/modelling/maps/bentham_ring/rock_bars_check.py measures it off the shipped .glb rather than asserting it. THE FIT (Ryan: "it just sticks right out the side and off the cliff"): built at world scale on an unscaled node, 11.92 x 8.5 m, its inner end on the cliff lip (never over the drop) and its outer end flaring out of the lane's outer wall and running on buried in it, filleted into floor and ceiling; origin the base centre, y=0 the ground, slots span local X, thickness along local Z. Slots are the old ones at world size, no opening over 0.48 m. ONE CONTIGUOUS MESH: the faces, the reveals and the caps all index one lattice of shared vertices, so components 1 and duplicate positions 0 come out of the topology, not out of a weld. TEXTURE: map 1's own rock through lib/texel.py, not an atlas (Ryan: "the texturing on the gate is bad, you seemed to fix it for the maps generally") -- map_base_build.py's rock and shade painters verbatim, the same seeds, the same tx.MPT 0.05 m per texel as map_base's walls, world-projected in the model's own frame ("box"), so marks run across face edges instead of each face carrying its own cut-off window. Two sheets and no more: map_base has a third, `ember`, and five glowing reveal faces did look good in here, but the Ring measures materials=16 on main against test_map_draw_budgets.gd's ceiling of 18, and a third material for ten triangles would spend the map's last slot on a detail the rock sheet's own emissive specks already carry. Two sheets is two surfaces; the node is unscaled, so the texels are 0.05 m in the world. RockBarsCollision is one box per rock column (floor to ceiling; the flare into the outer wall one per lattice lane) plus a sill under the lowest slot foot and a lintel over the highest slot head, shipped as a `-colonly` node: the slot lanes are left OPEN, which is what lets a round and a sight line through what a body cannot pass. Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `max_tris` counts only what is drawn.
